Every new key must read an NFC e-passport. The client checks the government signature inside the chip and the document key no second booklet shares, so one booklet yields one identity.

A booklet costs 120 dollars and four weeks, and the chip answers only when held against a phone, which puts each clone on a person somewhere on the mesa holding a document. Fifty clones run near 6,000 dollars and fifty in-person reads, against 40 dollars for fifty API keys today.

A juniper carries one seed per berry and quartz sets one lattice per crystal, so a farmer who wants fifty must grow fifty.
